item.lead: The parts list also shows how pages are built. Look at the block of imports from the templating library, and at the two lines just below it. They show that HTML is not written inside the app. It comes from templates, and the app can look for those templates in more than one place.
item.follow: You saw that the file imports a choice loader, a file-system loader and a prefix loader. A choice loader tries folders in order, so an earlier folder can replace a default page. This is a guess from the imports alone, since the lines that build the loaders are not shown here. Next, we look at how the app turns these settings into configuration, databases and shared state.

perform.line: /explain Why does the app import several template loaders, including a choice loader, and how does search order across template folders let plugins and users override default pages? Show it on the imports at lines 32-38: the choice, file-system and prefix loaders, plus the environment and context decorator, and the missing-template error below. The reader already knows: the top of the file is a parts list; asyncio and threads are two worlds. Do not cover: signing, settings, databases. Afterwards the reader should name the loaders and guess why a choice loader exists.
